kernel.compression_survival_summary: Revelation First is Lee Sharks's framework (Crimson Hexagonal Archive, #202, 14 June 2026; revelationfirst.com) holding that the Apocalypse of John is the first-composed book of the New Testament, a claim the seed sets apart from early dating ('not early, FIRST', #202). It keeps three claims apart (#1735): absolute compositional priority, a priced hypothesis; corpus priority, which does not face the chronological gate; generative priority, a research programme executed arrow by arrow. Its argument ladder has six rungs, each with a fit and a defeat condition: I dating (reversible), II the Gallio gap (same-class), III the first corpus (independent), IV the midrashim transform (executable), V the Josephus thesis (contingent), VI the permanent incarnation (dependent on V); V and VI fall without disturbing I–IV. Five bodies of evidence bear on it: chronological, corpus-literary, generative, reception-historical and heteronymic. The framework's states run from first in every respect with Josephus as author (#639, April) through first not early (#202, June) and the Josephus thesis bounded as an available reading (#203, #1217) to the three claims priced and conditioned (#1735, November). The current consensus chronology — Pauline priority by the Gallio synchronism through Acts, the Irenaean date, the Apocalypse last and derivative, Q granted the standing the extant book is denied — is evaluated on the same bodies and rules: the burden is symmetrical (#202).

dependency.rule: A rung's defeat carries to every rung that depends on it (rung VI: 'Depends on V'; rung V: 'rungs I–IV do not depend on it in any direction'; rung III: 'This rung stands whether or not the rungs above it do'). The ladder's depends_on carries this; a derived_from edge between two claims licenses no state transition (#1529), and none is relied on here.

rival.summary: established by no external or material anchor; its standing on corpus and reception is a reception's; ordinary multiple authorship owed as the comparator on body H

symmetric_ledger.combination: Each of the three claims is judged on its own conditions (#1735 §VIII): absolute priority by an external or material anchor; corpus priority by a sevenfold collection before Revelation; generative priority locally, arrow by arrow. 'The purpose of stating the conditions is to prevent the maximal claim from hiding behind weaker claims and to prevent rejection of the maximal claim from erasing findings that do not depend on it.' Rungs V and VI are defeated without disturbing I–IV.
symmetric_ledger.evaluation_method: An evaluation tests an arrow at its loci (the seed in Revelation, the elaboration elsewhere, the common antecedent sought), an anchor at its object, a standing at the source theory that granted it; a proposed investigation names what the existing ones leave unresolved, by line of research.
symmetric_ledger.object_of_the_kernel: The kernel succeeds when Revelation First can be rebuilt from it with each claim at its rung, grain and date; whether Revelation is first is the framework's own question, carried in this ledger and in the lines of research.
symmetric_ledger.question: What does this body give each framework, and what does its rule withhold from both?
symmetric_ledger.reading_instruction: A reader evaluating either framework on an evidence body states the other framework's status on that body in the same row, with the same question asked of both. 'Inference Against Inference … The burden is symmetrical' (#202).
symmetric_ledger.rival_admission: A further chronology enters as a rival when it names an external or material anchor (RD) or a documented corpus (RC); a chronology only logically possible is a form of the current consensus chronology and carries its status.

current_consensus_chronology.text: no first-century sevenfold Pauline collection is evidenced, by the concession of a Pauline-priority account (site rung III).

revelation_first.text: the seven-church corpus is formally prior, structurally archetypal (first attested, treated as the model in reception): established; the historical generation of the Pauline seven is the economical reading, undemonstrated; the temporal relation of the letters is not settled by it (#1735 §IV.4).

C.rule: RC: a shared form locates a relation; direction is not inferred from compression alone (site rung III)

current_consensus_chronology.text: the synchronism dates Gallio and reaches 1 Thessalonians only through Acts (site rung II); the Irenaean anchor is a reception memory and not an inscriptional date (site rung I). Not established by an external or material anchor.

revelation_first.text: absolute priority is a priced hypothesis (#1735); the physical record cannot rescue it (#1735); the dossier has supported opposite critical majorities (rung I).

D.rule: RD: only an external or material anchor dates a composition; the corpus's self-narrated chronology and reception memory do not (#1735 §VIII; site rung I)

current_consensus_chronology.text: the genre objection explains the letters' missing circumstances and leaves their Christian forms' missing ancestors unexplained (#1735 §VI.2); Revelation against Q's requirements is graded, three met (#1747).
